title: Ukraine's new missile can be launched from balloon, hit target in jammed area
text:
The DART missile is designed to overcome one of Russia's greatest battlefield advantages—its extensive electronic warfare (EW) capabilities.
A Ukrainian defense company is reportedly working on a missile that can be launched from a balloon. Reports have revealed that the missile can be launched from the the edge of the stratosphere and it can accurately hit target through jamming.
Developed by creators at Ukraine’s Center of Innovative Technologies Program, the DART missile is designed to overcome one of Russia’s greatest battlefield advantages—its extensive electronic warfare capabilities. The balloon carries the missile to an altitude of approximately 11–18 kilometres before releasing it. During its initial descent, DART relies on satellite navigation.
Once it reaches a lower altitude of around 6.5 kilometres, its navigation system deliberately shuts down, after which a solid-fuel rocketThis unusual flight profile is intended to make the missile largely immune to Russian electronic jamming. Since the missile no longer depends on satellite guidance during the final stage of its flight, enemy electronic warfare systems have limited ability to interfere with or divert it.
Unlike traditional cruise missiles, which require expensive launch platforms and sophisticated guidance throughout the mission, DART is designed as a relatively inexpensive strike option. Launching the weapon from a balloon significantly reduces the cost and complexity of deployment while also making it harder for air defence systems to detect its launch. The developers believe the system can deliver precision-guided payloads deep inside Russian territory while avoiding many of the challenges posed by dense electronic warfare environments.
Reports indicate that the current version of DART carries a warhead weighing roughly 10 kilograms . Instead of relying solely on explosive force, the payload disperses conductive graphite filaments intended to short-circuit electrical infrastructure, potentially causing temporary disruptions to power grids and military support networks. The weapon is still undergoing evaluation and has reportedly not yet completed Ukraine’s military certification process. The DART programme reflects Ukraine’s broader strategy of developing indigenous long-range strike capabilities.
Since Western partners have often placed restrictions on the use of supplied weapons against targets inside Russia, Kyiv has invested heavily in domestically produced drones and missiles capable of reaching strategic facilities hundreds of kilometres from the front lines, Recent Ukrainian strikes on oil refineries, military factories and logistics hubs have demonstrated an increasing ability to conduct deep attacks intended to disrupt Russia’s military infrastructure and impose economic costs.
